data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A small research team should adopt an existing experiment tracker only if their workflow is strictly observational; however, if the research involves active learning loops where the tracker must function as a real-time controller modifying experimental parameters, they must build a custom minimal tracker to avoid the 'integration tax' and causal fragility inherent in wrapping mismatched tools.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The team lacks the engineering bandwidth to maintain even a minimal custom state machine.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The active learning loop operates on a timescale (e.g., days per iteration) where API latency from existing tools is negligible.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The existing tool offers a native plugin architecture that exposes full control-plane access without abstraction leakage.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Control Theory Boundary: The mechanism distinguishes between passive data logging (observational) and active state modification (control). Existing tools optimize for schema flexibility and collaboration in observational modes but introduce latency and abstraction leaks when forced into a control loop. A custom build enforces a direct causal map between the agent's decision logic and the experimental apparatus, eliminating the 'integration tax' of hacking event-driven architectures to simulate control.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
